# Session Notes — 2026-08-14 — Muse Glimmer 30B (abandoned)

Attempted to add **Muse Glimmer 30B** (Meta, released ~10 August 2026) as a
fourth Task 1 answering pass, after Gemma 4, Cosmos-Reason2 and the dummy run.
Two complete pipelines were written and tested, both driven by
`query.routing.task1.json` — the first answering passes in this project to use
the routing file rather than sending every input to every query.

**Outcome: Muse Glimmer is not being used.** No answer was ever generated by
it. Neither pipeline completed a single inference call on this workstation, and
with the Answer Generation deadline on **17 August 2026** (recorded in
`SESSION.2026-08-12.answer-generation.md`) the remaining setup cost and the
projected multi-day single-GPU runtime ruled it out. The submitted runs remain
**Gemma 4** (`gemma4.run.task1.json`) and **Cosmos-Reason2**
(`cosmos.run.task1.json`), both already validated at 2,443/2,443.

The scripts are kept rather than deleted — they are finished and tested, and
the routing-driven design in them is reusable by any future model.

## 1. What Muse Glimmer is, and what it forced on the design

Checked against the model card, the Meta developer docs and the GGUF repo
before writing anything, because two properties decide the whole shape:

- **It takes images and text. There is no video path and no audio path.** A
  30B multimodal release, but a video reaches it exactly the way it reaches
  Gemma 4 — as extracted frames plus the Whisper transcript as text. The
  frames from `VQA/extract.frames.py` and the transcripts in
  `transcription_openwhisper/` were reused unchanged.
- **Reasoning strength is a controllable dial**: `low / medium / high / xhigh`.
  On the server path it travels as
  `chat_template_kwargs: {"reasoning_strength": ...}`; in transformers it is a
  kwarg of `apply_chat_template`. This is the property that made the routing
  file worth wiring in.
- Sampling per the model card: **temperature 1.0, top_p 0.95, top_k 64** —
  deliberately not the lowered temperature `generate.answers.py` uses for
  Gemma 4, because there is no ensemble vote here to concentrate.

Confirmed from the GGUF header directly (`general.architecture = muse-glimmer`):
52 blocks, 6656 embedding, 32 heads / **2 KV heads**, key/value length 128,
131,072 context, `final_logit_softcapping 20.0`, a per-layer sliding-window
pattern, and `file_type 15` = `MOSTLY_Q4_K_M`. The KV geometry gives
**~52 KiB per token**, so a 32k window costs ~1.7 GB of KV and the full 131k
costs ~7 GB — the latter does not fit beside 15.6 GB of weights on a 24 GB
card. The published `-c 131072` invocation is not runnable on this box.

---

## 2. The routed design (shared by both scripts)

`Pipeline` from `query.routing.task1.json` maps directly onto request contents.
This is the first pipeline here that does not send everything to everything:

| Routing step | Effect | Queries |
|---|---|---|
| `frames` | attach images | 2,338 of 2,443 |
| `asr_transcript` | attach the Whisper transcript | 576 |
| `dense_timestamped_frames` | send every extracted frame instead of subsampling to 16 | 886 |
| `frame_ocr` | add the read-text-on-screen rule | 57 |
| `reasoning_prompt` | raise reasoning strength | folded into the policy below |

Reasoning strength is derived from the router's `Inference` and `Temporal`
flags, and the generation budget moves with it:

| `(inference, temporal)` | strength | max tokens | queries |
|---|---|---|---|
| neither | low | 2,048 | 721 |
| one of the two | medium | 4,096 | 1,422 |
| both | high | 8,192 | 300 |

Total images that would be sent: **31,305**, max 32 per query.
`--ignore-routing` sends frames and transcript to every query at a fixed
strength — the ablation the routed run would have had to beat.

Design details worth keeping:

- **Frames are interleaved with `[mm:ss]` labels**, one text block per image,
  rather than sent as a single block. A frames-as-video model cannot ground a
  "when does X happen" question otherwise, and 886 queries are temporal.
- **Work is grouped by (video, dense, strength)** so queries sharing a prompt
  prefix run back to back — 2,289 groups over 2,443 queries.
- **No query is ever sent with zero evidence.** The router sends 168 queries to
  the audio alone; when such a video turns out to have no transcript, the
  frames are restored rather than sending a prompt that says "answer from the
  transcript" followed by "the video has no detected speech". This was found by
  inspecting real mock output, not by reasoning about the code.
- Output format, cache/resume, `--rebuild`, `--only`, `--force`, tidy/dedupe
  and the fallback answer pool are identical to `generate.answers.cosmos.py`,
  so the runs would have been directly comparable.

## 3. Path A — llama.cpp server: what blocked it

| # | Blocker | Status |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | `llama-server` on PATH resolved to a **winget CPU-only build (b9038)**, not the CUDA build in the directory the shell was sitting in. PowerShell does not search the current directory. Produced `no usable GPU found ... compiled without GPU support`. | Diagnosed; fix is `.\llama-server.exe` |
| 2 | Model path was passed relative, resolving against the llama.cpp directory rather than `E:\TREC_2026\models\` | Diagnosed |
| 3 | The local CUDA build was **b9050**, which predates Muse Glimmer support. Support merged 10 Aug 2026 ([PR #26841](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/26841)), first shipped in **b10353**; latest at the time was b10413. Confirmed locally: `llama.dll` and `mtmd.dll` contain no `muse-glimmer` string (they do contain `qwen3vl`, `gemma3`), so the load would have failed with `unknown model architecture`. | Not resolved — upgrade never performed |
| 4 | Only **9.2 GB of the 24 GB card was free**: the Cosmos-Reason2 vLLM server was still running in WSL2 after ~7 h with `--gpu-memory-utilization 0.75`. Weights + mmproj need ~17 GB. | Diagnosed; the Cosmos run was already complete and validated, so the server was safe to stop |
| 5 | `-c 131072` from the model card is not survivable here (see §1) | Diagnosed; `-c 32768` recommended |

None of these are fundamental. The path was abandoned before the llama.cpp
upgrade was done, in favour of the native-Python route.

---

## 4. Path B — native transformers: what blocked it

`transformers 5.15.0` was **already installed and already had the model** —
`MuseGlimmerForConditionalGeneration`, `AutoModelForMultimodalLM`, and four
registered architectures (`muse_glimmer`, `_assistant`, `_text`, `_vision`).
No upgrade needed. The obstacles were elsewhere:

- **There is no Ampere-compatible quantized checkpoint.** The bf16 repo is
  **59.6 GB**. Every transformers-native quant on the Hub is FP8-block (needs
  sm_89+), NVFP4 (needs Blackwell) or MLX (Apple only); this box is an
  **RTX 3090, sm_86**. So the only route was the full bf16 download plus
  **bitsandbytes NF4** at load time — and NF4 is uncalibrated round-to-nearest,
  whereas the GGUF that was already on disk was Meta's calibrated, mixed-
  precision Q4_K_M. The native path was therefore *starting from a worse 4-bit*
  and paying 59.6 GB for the privilege.
- `llama-cpp-python` was considered and rejected: latest release **0.3.34 (12
  July 2026)** predates Muse support, and building from source is not possible
  here — VS 2019 is installed **without the C++ workload** (`vswhere` returns
  nothing for `VC.Tools.x86.x64`, no `cl.exe`).
- The 55.5 GB checkpoint **was downloaded** (2 shards, completed 10:57).
- The run then failed on a **missing `torchvision`** —
  `MuseGlimmerImageProcessor` is torchvision-backed with no slow fallback. The
  venv had torch 2.6.0+cu124 and torchaudio but never torchvision. Fix is
  `torchvision==0.21.0 --index-url .../cu124`, pinned because an unpinned
  install declares a newer `torch==` and would replace the +cu124 build the
  rest of the project depends on.

That was the point at which Muse was dropped. The install itself is trivial;
what it would have bought was the *start* of a run, not a finished one.

---

## 5. Why it was not possible here

To be precise about the record: **no single hard blocker was ever proven.**
Every obstacle in §3 and §4 had a known fix. What made it not viable on this
workstation was the combination:

- **One 3090, one model, no room to share it.** At 24 GB, Muse Glimmer at 4-bit
  leaves ~7 GB for KV and activations, and the card is also what Cosmos and
  Ollama use. Nothing else can run while it does.
- **Projected runtime does not fit the deadline.** Decode dominates: reasoning
  traces of a few hundred to a few thousand tokens across 2,443 queries. On
  bitsandbytes NF4 — which dequantizes per matmul, against llama.cpp's fused
  Q4_K kernels — an order-of-magnitude estimate is *tens of hours at best, over
  100 hours at worst*. With answers due 17 August and two validated runs
  already in hand, a multi-day single-GPU job with no measured throughput
  behind it was not a defensible use of the remaining time.
- **Accumulated setup still outstanding:** llama.cpp upgrade (path A) or
  torchvision plus a first successful load and a smoke test (path B), before
  any timing number would even exist.

The honest summary is that Muse Glimmer is *runnable* on this hardware in
principle and was not runnable on this hardware *in the time available*.

---

## 6. What was verified before it was dropped

Neither script is untested; both were exercised end to end with the model
replaced by a stand-in, since the real model never loaded.

- **Server path**: driven against a mock `llama-server` that recorded every
  request. Confirmed routing plans, frame subsampling, `[mm:ss]` interleaving,
  base64 data URIs, `chat_template_kwargs`, per-strength token budgets,
  resume/`--rebuild`/`--force`/`--only`, and tolerant JSON extraction when the
  model wraps prose around its answer.
- **Native path**: driven with the model and JPEG decode stubbed. Same coverage,
  plus a **reasoning-strength probe** — `apply_chat_template` forwards unknown
  kwargs into the jinja context instead of rejecting them, so a template that
  did not consume `reasoning_strength` would silently run every query at the
  default. The probe renders `low` and `xhigh` and compares; tested against
  templates that consume, ignore and reject the kwarg.
- **Both** emit run entries that `validate.ag.run.py` accepts with no format
  errors (only the expected "missing queries" on a partial run).
- Two real defects were found and fixed this way: the zero-evidence prompt
  described in §2, and a stray blank line before the routed extra rules.

Also added after the fact, because each surfaced as an unhelpful traceback: a
checkpoint guard (a missing or half-downloaded local path otherwise reaches
huggingface_hub and returns `HFValidationError: Repo id must use alphanumeric
chars`, an error about entirely the wrong thing), and a dependency preflight
that reports all four lazily-imported requirements at once with the correct
pinned install lines.

## 8. If this is picked up again

Fastest route to a first token, in order:

1. `wsl -d Ubuntu-24.04 -- pkill -f vllm` — frees ~15 GB the Cosmos server is
   still holding.
2. Prefer the **llama.cpp path**: download build ≥ b10353 (the local one is
   b9050), run `.\llama-server.exe` with absolute paths, `--mmproj`, `--jinja`,
   and `-c 32768`. It keeps Meta's calibrated quant and its fused kernels, and
   the GGUF is only 17 GB to re-download against 56 GB already spent on bf16.
3. Confirm the startup line reports `vision True` — a server without `--mmproj`
   accepts image content, drops it, and answers plausibly from the text alone.
4. `--limit 20` first. The per-strength timings it prints are the only number
   that decides whether the full 2,443 is affordable; everything in §5 is an
   estimate until that exists.

The routing-driven design, the `[mm:ss]` interleaving and the strength policy
are model-agnostic and worth lifting into any future answering pass.
